title: Merchandise placement

location.series: IBM Logo and Brand Guidelines for Third Parties / copyright 2022

slide_intent: Show identity relationships at object scale, because logo placement and nearby partner marks change how merchandise communicates affiliation.
strategic_value: A relationship tagline and considered placement can make IBM’s role clearer on co-branded reusable items.
demonstration: A four-panel grid pairs a shirt and tote above crossed-out disposable-cup and wall-plug examples; several mockups are labeled FPO.
practical_value: Use the examples to evaluate placement and relationship text, while treating FPO artwork as placeholders.

content_islands.name: Heading
content_islands.spec: Place Merchandise placement at upper left.

content_islands.name: Reusable examples
content_islands.spec: Place shirt and tote mockups across the upper row with captions about placement and mandatory relationship taglines for two or more logos.

content_islands.name: Rejected items
content_islands.spec: Place the disposable cup and wall-plug item below with diagonal rejection lines and red captions.

ingredient.name: Co-branded merchandise relationship
ingredient.role: Explain the affiliation between marks on a shared physical object.
ingredient.application: Consider placement, size and neighboring logos; include a relationship tagline whenever two or more logos are required.
ingredient.scope: Promotional merchandise in this guide. Mockups marked FPO are placeholders; the page rejects disposable and wall-socket items.

reference_purposes.Application: The shirt and tote examples demonstrate the object-level placement judgment and relationship-text requirement.
reference_purposes.Constraint: A relationship tagline is mandatory when two or more logos appear; disposable and wall-socket items are prohibited on this page.
